newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt approves tariff cuts for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt approves tariff cuts for 1997.

text.p: The Czech government on Wednesday approved a tariff list for 1997 which lowers the average tariff burden to 3.2 percent from 3.8 percent this year, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said.
Speaking to reporters after a regular cabinet session, Kocarnik said the lower tariffs will take about 2.5 billion crowns out of the state's revenues.
He said, however, that the state still hopes to collect just under 20 billion crowns on tariffs in 1997 -- compared with this year's 20.3 billion -- as imports rise.
He said the general decrease in tariffs was in accordance with the association agreement with the European Union and other free-trade agreements.
Kocarnik said that 70 percent of industrial goods imported from the EU will be completely tariff-free next year.
